Illustration of programming parameters such as fiber length, fiber volume, SMC output and fiber feed rate versus blade speed. 18 Figure 19 illustrates early trials with 30 wt% glass SMC produced with the setup described in the earlier sections. Uniform quality SMC with good glass fiber wet out was produced. When switching the line to produce carbon SMC, the 450k Kaltex precursor TCF was used. The cut quality of the carbon fiber was very uniform as shown in Figure 20. However, the wet-out of the carbon fiber SMC was not optimal. Figure 21 illustrates that the core fibers remained dry despite passing through the compaction zone. Several trials were run by lowering the line speed from 8 ft/min to 3 ft/min. Still the core remained dry. Through team discussions it was determined that a higher engagement compaction zone would be needed. This led to re-engineering several portions of the line, and hence this is referred to as SMC-V2 (SMC version 2). Figure 19. Example of finished product. The core of the carbon SMC remained dry in the SMC-V1 20 SMC V2 (SMC Version 2) Based on the process trials run with the SMC-V1 several changes had to be incorporated in the SMC-V2. This update took approximately 5 months to engineer and implement. The aspects of the changes are:  Some of the fibers entering the cutting zone remained hanging analogous to cantilever beams. The hanging of the fibers resulting in their bending and hence causing non-uniform fiber lengths with a larger standard deviation. To overcome this the fiber tension was increased and overhanging distance was minimized to bring the fiber taut as it entered the cutting zone.
